title: Middle Node of a Chain
statement:
You get the head of a non-empty singly linked list. Return its middle node.

If the list has an even number of nodes there are two middle nodes; return the second of them.

In tests a list is written as an array of its values, and the returned node is shown as the list that starts at it. For [1, 2, 3] the answer prints as [2, 3].

examples.why: Five nodes: the third one, 9, is in the middle, with two nodes on each side.
Four nodes: 3 and 9 are both middles, and the rule picks the second. Stopping the fast pointer one step early would return 3.

hints: Counting the nodes first and then walking half way works. Can you do it in a single walk?
Move two pointers from the head: one by one node per step, the other by two.
When the fast pointer falls off the end (it or its next is null), the slow pointer is on the middle. Check which middle you land on for an even length.

explain.intuition:
Two runners start at the head. The slow one takes one step at a time, the fast one two. When the fast runner reaches the end, the slow one has covered exactly half the distance, so it stands on the middle.

The loop condition decides which middle you get for even lengths. Looping while fast and fast.next both exist gives the second middle: with 4 nodes, fast goes 1 → 3 → past the end while slow goes 1 → 2 → 3. Looping while fast.next and fast.next.next exist gives the first middle instead, which is what you want when splitting a list for merge sort.
steps: While fast and fast.next are not null: slow = slow.next, fast = fast.next.next.
pitfalls: Using the first-middle loop condition and returning node 2 of 4 instead of node 3.
Checking only fast.next, which crashes when fast itself becomes null on even lengths.

solutions.title: Count, then walk half way
solutions.idea: One pass to count n, a second to step n / 2 (rounded down) times from the head.

solutions.title: Slow and fast pointers
solutions.idea: One pointer moves one step, the other two. When the fast one runs out, the slow one is in the middle.

followups: Return the first middle instead for even lengths. What changes in the loop?
Use the same two pointers to check whether the list is a palindrome in O(1) extra space.
